title: A thioridazine-derived molecule exhibits potential anti-inflammatory activity through IKK inhibition.
authors: Sarup, Shivmuni; Atre, Rajat; Obukhov, Alexander G; Tabrez, Shams; Yadav, Priyanka; Kshatri, Aravind Singh; Sk, M Hassan; Alamri, Abdulaziz; Khan, Mohd Shahnawaz; Baig, Mirza S
one_liner_zh: 该文研究硫利达嗪衍生物通过IKK抑制发挥抗炎作用，核心是蛋白-小分子药物设计，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Chronic inflammatory diseases are leading causes of morbidity and mortality, necessitating the development of targeted therapeutics with improved safety. Many drugs have been withdrawn from the market because of their off-target effects, particularly hERG inhibition, which leads to severe cardiotoxicity. The NF-kappaB pathway plays a critical role in inflammation and immune response, making IKKbeta an attractive therapeutic target. Thioridazine, a known inhibitor of IKKbeta, has demonstrated potential anti-inflammatory effects. However, its clinical utility is severely limited by the strong inhibition of the hERG potassium channel, which increases the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Therefore, it is necessary to develop safer IKKbeta inhibitors using rational drug design approaches. By leveraging a similar compound library and in silico techniques, we aimed to retain the original therapeutic potential of thioridazine, while minimising its drawbacks. A library of thioridazine derivatives was computationally designed and screened by molecular docking and simulations. The selected compounds were subjected to patch-clamp analysis, confocal microscopy, western blotting, and qRT-PCR to evaluate their anti-inflammatory potential and hERG affinity, respectively. TDZ-D210-(2-oxo-2-pyrrolidin-1-ylethyl)acridin-9-one, a thioridazine derivative, displayed significantly lower hERG binding while maintaining strong IKKbeta inhibition, preserving IkappaBalpha stability, reducing NF-kappaB p65 translocation, and suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. This study highlights the potential of ligand-based lead optimisation techniques for mitigating off-target effects, thereby offering a safer anti-inflammatory therapeutic candidate. By overcoming the cardiotoxicity associated with thioridazine, TDZ-D2 presents a promising avenue for drug development for inflammatory diseases.
abstract_zh: 慢性炎症性疾病是发病率和死亡率的主要原因，因此需要开发具有更高安全性的靶向治疗药物。许多药物因其脱靶效应，特别是hERG抑制，导致严重的心脏毒性，已从市场撤回。NF-kappaB通路在炎症和免疫反应中发挥关键作用，使IKKbeta成为有吸引力的治疗靶点。硫利达嗪（Thioridazine）作为IKKbeta的已知抑制剂，已显示出潜在的抗炎效果。然而，其临床实用性受到hERG钾通道强烈抑制的严重限制，这增加了心律失常的风险。因此，有必要利用合理的药物设计方法开发更安全的IKKbeta抑制剂。通过利用相似的化合物库和计算机模拟技术，我们旨在保留硫利达嗪原有的治疗潜力，同时最小化其缺点。我们计算设计了一个硫利达嗪衍生物库，并通过分子对接和模拟进行筛选。选定的化合物分别通过膜片钳分析、共聚焦显微镜、蛋白质印迹和qRT-PCR评估其抗炎潜力和hERG亲和力。TDZ-D210-(2-氧代-2-吡咯烷-1-基乙基)吖啶-9-酮，一种硫利达嗪衍生物，显示出显著较低的hERG结合，同时保持强效的IKKbeta抑制，维持IkappaBalpha稳定性，减少NF-kappaB p65转位，并抑制促炎细胞因子表达。本研究强调了基于配体的先导化合物优化技术在减轻脱靶效应方面的潜力，从而提供更安全的抗炎治疗候选药物。通过克服与硫利达嗪相关的心脏毒性，TDZ-D2为炎症性疾病的药物开发提供了有前景的途径。
